claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have one child, Alex, who's 16 and lives with me at home. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I understand you have a 16-year-old child named Alex who lives with you.

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask: Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. They're studying for their A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 16 and studying for A-levels, I need to confirm a few more details.

When did Alex turn 16, or when will they turn 16? (I need to know the specific date or at least which month and year)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex turned 16 back in March of this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. And when did Alex start their A-level course? (I need to know which month and year they began this education)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: They started in September, just a few months ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Just to clarify - did Alex start their A-levels in September of this year (the same year they turned 16 in March)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - they turned 16 in March and then started their A-levels in September of this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying. Now I need to ask a few questions about your own circumstances:

Are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great, thank you. And are you the person primarily responsible for Alex? In other words, are you the main person who looks after Alex and meets their everyday needs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me and I'm the one who looks after them day-to-day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Do you or Alex receive any other benefits or support that might affect Child Benefit eligibility, such as Income Support, Universal Credit, or any disability benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of us receives any benefits like that at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question: Do you (or your partner, if you have one) have an individual income over £50,000 per year? 

(This won't affect whether you're eligible to claim Child Benefit, but it may affect whether there's a tax charge if you do claim it - I just want to make sure I give you complete information)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, my income is well below that threshold, so that shouldn't be an issue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 16 and in approved education (A-levels), which means you can continue claiming Child Benefit for them
- Child Benefit can be claimed for young people aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training
- You live in the UK and are Alex's primary carer
- Your income is below £50,000, so you won't face the High Income Child Benefit Charge

**Important note:** You can continue to receive Child Benefit for Alex until they turn 20, or until they leave approved education or training - whichever comes first. This means Child Benefit will continue as long as Alex stays in their A-level course and any subsequent approved education (like university).

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit online or by post. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask!
